comparison: Both strongly support the GWA findings for Erysiphales resistance (C10, C90-C99, C130-C134). OpenEval notes genome-wide significance and enrichment validation but acknowledges lack of functional validation. Peer reviewers praised the mapping to defense genes and accepted the weaker M. persicae results without seeing them as undermining conclusions.

Both support the climate-resistance correlations (C5, C7, C78-C81, C122-C124). OpenEval marks C81 as speculative regarding mechanistic explanation. Peer reviewers accepted the correlational findings and the speculative interpretation about warmer climate evolution without criticism.

Both support the heritability estimates (C3-C4, C71-C76). OpenEval emphasizes the statistical rigor with confidence intervals and validation of reference genome mapping over MG-RAST. Peer reviewers noted relatively high heritabilities support the authors' arguments and praised statistical enhancements in the revised manuscript.

Both support the glucosinolate correlations (C6, C84-C88, C125-C129). OpenEval notes statistical significance and mechanistic interpretations supported by literature but acknowledges speculation. Peer reviewers accepted the biochemical correlations without challenge, finding them consistent with A. thaliana literature.

Both support the species identification findings (C62-C70, C120). OpenEval emphasizes the methodological soundness of competitive mapping and high confidence percentages. Peer reviewers accepted technical findings without challenge and praised methodological clarifications in the revised manuscript.

Both address methylation findings (C12-C14, C102-C109, C142-C144) but with different emphases. OpenEval supports the DMR findings while acknowledging the relaxed FDR threshold and inability to distinguish inherited vs. induced methylation. Peer reviewers marked this as UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about validation and causal links, noting more cautious interpretation in revisions.

Both support the novelty claims (C150-C152). OpenEval notes the substantial nature of the coupled approach while acknowledging the novelty claim cannot be fully verified. Peer reviewers strongly endorsed the novelty and significance, with the editor calling it 'a significant methodological advance' and the first coupled GWA-EWA claim was not challenged.

Both strongly support the methodological innovation (C16, C116-C118, C153). OpenEval validates the approach through multiple lines of evidence while acknowledging potential applications. Peer reviewers explicitly praised this as a significant methodological advance, with all reviewers noting the innovative use of unmapped reads.

Both support the ambiguous read removal methodology (C57-C61, C89, C119, C135, C137). OpenEval provides detailed quantitative validation showing elimination of false GWA peaks. Peer reviewers strongly endorsed this improvement, stating it should be adopted more widely and praising increased transparency in data handling.

Both address MAPKKK20 and methylation associations (C110-C115, C145-C146, C148-C149). OpenEval supports the statistical validation while noting C148 is speculative and mechanistic validation is lacking. Peer reviewers also noted inflated p-values for M. persicae and emphasized the associative nature of findings, with concerns about causal links.

Both support the negative finding on maternal effects (C77). OpenEval notes this appropriately rules out maternal effects. Peer reviewers accepted this negative result without challenge, though it was not a focus of discussion.

Partial overlap on validation and contributions (C154-C156). OpenEval R9 discusses empirical validation showing geographic structure and associations. Peer R10 endorses the novelty and significance of results with potential implications for many systems.

OpenEval supports the experimental design details (C1-C2, C159-C163), noting substantial sample size and appropriate common garden design. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these experimental design claims.

OpenEval supports the limitation acknowledgment regarding inherited vs. induced methylation (C138-C141), noting honest assessment of interpretational constraints. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these limitation claims, though peer R8 touches on related causal uncertainty issues.
